ladder.teaches: paths and costs on a grid
ladder.why: The smallest grid DP: paths into a cell come only from above and from the left, so you add those two counts.

ladder.teaches: paths and costs on a grid
ladder.why: The same recurrence with costs instead of counts: take the cheaper of the two ways in, and keep one rolling row.
The two-prefix table: a match extends the diagonal, a mismatch drops one character from either string.
Insert, delete and replace become the three neighbouring cells of the LCS-shaped table, with base cases i and j.

ladder.teaches: palindromes: DP over (i, j) of one string
ladder.why: DP over the ends (i, j) of one string: equal ends wrap the inside answer, otherwise drop one end.

ladder.teaches: design the state for two sequences
ladder.why: Pick the state 'how much of the pattern is matched so far' and count ways, sweeping slots high to low so one character fills one slot.

ladder.teaches: design the state for two sequences
ladder.why: Two strings with different rules (subsequence in x, substring in y): the state must encode a substring ending at j, so mismatches carry down instead of resetting.

ladder.teaches: paths and costs on a grid
ladder.why: A grid DP whose state is a shape: the largest square ending at a corner is 1 + the min of three neighbours.

ladder.teaches: paths and costs on a grid
ladder.why: Grid costs plus a layer index (which grid you are on), showing how to add a dimension when the story adds a choice.

ladder.teaches: paths and costs on a grid
ladder.why: A non-rectangular grid that is easiest bottom-up, where the edge cases disappear.

ladder.teaches: design the state for two sequences
ladder.why: An OA counting question that becomes 'latest start that still matches target[0..j]', a two-sequence state updated as s is scanned.
An Amazon OA story that is n - LCS, where unique values let the LCS shrink to a longest increasing subsequence.

ladder.teaches: palindromes: DP over (i, j) of one string
ladder.why: Palindrome (i, j) DP on the concatenation, read only at outer pairs that straddle the two words.

notes: Edit distance has only one rung (the classic itself); the pool's other edit-distance-titled problems are either duplicates or BFS (word ladder). google-count-all-one-squares was taken from outside the pools (in no other pool). salesforce-closest-subsequence-sum moved from this pool to knapsack. amazon-minimum-insertions has a garbled source statement and no constraints; the repair rewrites both, and its single example is consistent.
